study_focus: Anatomical directional terms and body systems
Common prefixes, suffixes, and root words
Clinical abbreviations used in physician notes
domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the medical terminology and anatomy coders must recognize to interpret provider documentation. It underpins accurate code selection across every other domain on the CPC exam.

study_focus: Office and outpatient E/M level selection
Inpatient and consultation visit codes
Documentation of history, exam, and medical decision making
domain_guidance.summary: Evaluation and Management focuses on selecting the correct office, hospital, and other E/M visit levels based on documentation. Coders must apply current MDM or time-based criteria to determine the appropriate code.

study_focus: Anesthesia time and base unit calculation
Physical status modifiers P1 through P6
Qualifying circumstance add-on codes
domain_guidance.summary: Anesthesia covers formula-based calculation of anesthesia time units, base units, modifiers, and qualifying circumstance codes. It tests familiarity with anesthesia terminology and physical status modifiers used on physician claims.

study_focus: Integumentary and musculoskeletal procedure codes
Cardiovascular and digestive system sections
Surgical package and global period rules
domain_guidance.summary: Surgery spans multiple CPT sections including integumentary, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, and digestive systems. It is the largest procedural area on the CPC and demands section-specific code knowledge across many body systems.

study_focus: Diagnostic imaging code selection by modality
Professional and technical component modifiers 26 and TC
Radiation oncology and nuclear medicine codes
domain_guidance.summary: Radiology covers diagnostic and therapeutic imaging codes across all modalities. Coders must distinguish professional versus technical components and apply contrast and supervision rules correctly on imaging claims accurately.

study_focus: Organ or disease-oriented panel codes
Surgical pathology and cytopathology coding
Molecular and genetic testing codes
domain_guidance.summary: Pathology and Laboratory covers diagnostic studies, panels, and anatomic pathology services. It requires understanding of panel component rules and specimen-based coding for accurate claim submission in clinical settings.

study_focus: Immunization and vaccine administration codes
Dialysis and cardiology service coding
Hydration, infusion, and injection coding
domain_guidance.summary: Medicine covers non-surgical diagnostic and therapeutic services such as immunizations, dialysis, and cardiology procedures. It also includes HCPCS Level II drug administration codes for outpatient settings in primary care.

study_focus: Durable medical equipment and supply codes
HCPCS Level II modifier application
Temporary and quarterly updated HCPCS codes
domain_guidance.summary: HCPCS Level II covers codes for supplies, equipment, and services not included in CPT. Coders must apply correct modifiers and understand temporary Q, S, and K code categories.

study_focus: Alphabetic Index and Tabular List navigation
Chapter-specific coding guidelines
Principal diagnosis selection rules
domain_guidance.summary: ICD-10-CM Diagnosis Coding tests application of the current Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting. Coders must sequence correctly and follow chapter-specific rules for accurate code assignment in clinical practice.

study_focus: Modifier 25, 59, and 22 usage
Bilateral, multiple procedure, and assistant surgeon modifiers
Modifier documentation requirements
domain_guidance.summary: CPT Modifiers tests correct two-digit modifier appendage to procedure and E/M codes. Misapplied modifiers are a common reason for claim denial and exam failure on the CPC.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive early with two forms of ID and your AAPC membership card. Budget your 340 minutes across 100 questions, leaving time to review flagged items. Read each stem fully before selecting an answer.

faq.answer_text: The passing score for the CPC exam is 70 percent. AAPC scores the exam against this benchmark, and candidates must meet or exceed it to earn the credential.

faq.answer_text: The CPC exam allows 340 minutes of testing time. Candidates should pace themselves across all 100 questions and reserve minutes at the end for review.

methodology.summary: This page was built from AAPC official exam guides and the FY 2025 ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting. Domain summaries were mapped directly to AAPC's published content areas.

editorial.overview: The Certified Professional Coder (CPC) exam is administered by AAPC and tests working knowledge of medical coding across physician-office settings. It spans 10 content domains including CPT, ICD-10-CM, and HCPCS Level II. Candidates answer 100 multiple-choice questions in a linear format, drawing on applied knowledge of procedure and diagnosis code sets used in outpatient and physician-based environments.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Build a study plan that walks each of the 10 domains in order, using the current ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines as your anchor for diagnosis questions. Practice with timed 100-question sets to build pacing for the 340-minute window. Review CPT modifier rules and E/M documentation criteria separately, since these trip up even experienced coders.
skills_summary: Apply ICD-10-CM diagnosis coding conventions and guidelines
Assign CPT procedure codes across surgery, radiology, and medicine
Use HCPCS Level II codes for supplies and services
Apply CPT modifiers correctly to procedure claims
Determine Evaluation and Management levels from documentation
Code anesthesia, pathology, and laboratory services accurately
editorial.who_should_take: Medical coders, billing specialists, and health information students preparing for outpatient and physician-based coding roles should take the CPC. It suits those with hands-on CPT, ICD-10-CM, and HCPCS Level II experience seeking AAPC credentialing.

exam_price_notes: AAPC member price $299. Non-member $399. Annual AAPC membership ~$199.
exam_rules: Open-book for coding manuals (ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS Level II code books). Physical books only — no electronic or online resources. Tabs and highlighting allowed in code books. Scratch paper provided. Proctor monitors via webcam.
id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required. Name must match AAPC account registration.
